name: Monastic Vows (Hermetic)
description: Major Hermetic Flaw: vows of poverty, chastity and obedience; the magus cannot own vis, possesses only functional magic devices, and may be barred from binding a familiar. All Neriusians take it.

name: Pagan
description: Major Supernatural Story Flaw for a character who does not follow the Church, has never been baptized, and may suffer supernatural consequences from Christian worship.

name: Unbaptized
description: Major Story Flaw for a Christian never baptized, perhaps to preserve a supernatural nature; they gain no benefit from the sacraments.

name: Enemies
description: Flaw taken by Perfecti as Enemies (the Church), a Major Story Flaw.

name: Dhimmi
description: Minor General Flaw reflecting the status of non-Muslims living under Muslim rule.

name: Outsider
description: Major Social Status Flaw that Muslim characters living in non-Muslim lands should always take.

name: Proud
description: Personality Flaw carried by the Church Deacon grog template.

name: Higher Purpose
description: Flaw carried by the Church Deacon and Franciscan Teacher templates.

name: Busybody
description: Flaw of the Curious Nun template, who meddles in other grogs' affairs.

name: Incomprehensible
description: Flaw of the Curious Nun template.

name: Dutybound
description: Flaw of the Pious Warrior template, whose sense of duty prevents dishonorable conduct.

name: Pious
description: Flaw of the Pious Warrior template.

name: Favors
description: Flaw of the Byzantine Priest, who owes many favors to those who helped him.

name: Generous
description: Major Flaw of the Byzantine Priest template.

name: Fear
description: Flaw of the Byzantine Priest template (fear of fire).

name: No Sense of Direction
description: Flaw of the Byzantine Priest template.

name: Black Sheep
description: Flaw of the Knight Templar template, estranged from his family.

name: Greedy
description: Flaw of the Knight Templar template, who cannot resist fine living.

name: Disfigured
description: Flaw of the Knight Templar template, who bears a frightening facial scar.

name: Ambitious
description: Flaw of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Ars Notoria (Virtue)
description: Major Supernatural Virtue granting the Ars Notoria Ability; only Gifted magi, academics and clerics may start with it.

name: Perfectus
description: Mythic Companion Virtue required for Perfecti characters.

name: Purity
description: Holy Virtue/Ability favored by the Neriusians and required of Perfecti; used for ceremonial casting of The Neriusian Portal.

name: Second Sight
description: Virtue that Perfecti begin with.

name: Transcendence
description: Holy Virtue and Ability that Perfecti begin with.

name: Clerk
description: Social Status Virtue of the Church Deacon template.

name: Student of Dominion
description: Virtue granting a bonus to Dominion Lore, held by the Church Deacon.

name: Student of the Divine
description: Virtue granting a bonus to Dominion Lore, held by the Byzantine Priest and Knight Templar.

name: Failed Monk
description: Social Status Virtue of the Curious Nun (as Failed Nun).

name: Magic Sensitivity
description: Virtue and Ability of the Curious Nun, used to sense auras.

name: Arcane Lore
description: Virtue held by the Curious Nun template.

name: Intuition
description: Virtue held by the Curious Nun template.

name: Covenfolk
description: Social Status Virtue of the Pious Warrior template.

name: Relic
description: Virtue of the Pious Warrior, who wears a cross-shaped saintly relic that protects him.

name: Warrior
description: Virtue of the Pious Warrior template.

name: Eastern Priest
description: Social Status Virtue of the Byzantine Priest template.

name: Brother Knight
description: Social Status Virtue of the Knight Templar template.

name: Ceremony
description: Holy Virtue held by the Knight Templar template.

name: Improved Characteristics
description: Virtue held by the Knight Templar template.

name: Puissant Single Weapon
description: Virtue held by the Knight Templar template.

name: Mendicant Friar
description: Social Status Virtue of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Magister in Artibus
description: Virtue of the Franciscan Teacher, who graduated university as a master of arts.

name: Puissant Teaching
description: Virtue of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Good Teacher
description: Virtue of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Inspirational
description: Virtue of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Greater Purifying Touch
description: Supernatural Major Virtue granted free by the Third Ring of Solomon, curing one chosen disease.

name: Patron Angel
description: Major General Virtue granted by the Fourth Ring of Solomon; a personal angel acting as guide and teacher.

name: Guardian Angel
description: Virtue whose powers the Patron Angel summoned by the Fourth Ring possesses.

name: Sense Holiness and Unholiness
description: Divine supernatural Virtue/Ability to feel good and evil; the Fifth Ring of Solomon acts similarly but identifies realms exactly.

name: Commanding Aura
description: Blessed-by-God power with which hidden Fatimid imams would be endowed.

name: Ars Notoria
description: Academic, Arcane, Supernatural Ability of divine orations and rituals descended from King Solomon, granting divine wisdom through rings of recitation.

name: Holy Music
description: Ability of the Holy Method of Meditation allowing a supernatural state of mind by singing praises to God.

name: Holy Magic
description: Favored Ability of the Priory of Saint Nerius.

name: Intervention
description: Holy Ability favored by the Cantores and Neriusians, used in ceremonial casting.

name: Premonitions
description: Favored Ability of the Priory of Saint Nerius.

name: Blessing
description: Favored Ability of the Cantores.

name: Enchanting Music
description: Supernatural Ability; a true Cantor's songs are said to be similar in power.

name: Church Lore
description: Ability required of Perfecti and used by church-connected templates.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Arcane Ability of knowledge about the Dominion, required of Perfecti.

name: Divine Lore
description: Lore Ability used to find a copy of Ars Notoria; subject of the text to unGifted readers.

name: Theology
description: Academic Ability; the Second Ring of Solomon grants 100 experience points in it.

name: Theology: Islam
description: New Academic Knowledge for Muslim characters.

name: Islamic Law
description: New Academic Knowledge for Muslim characters.

name: Philosophiae
description: Academic Ability; the First Ring of Solomon grants 100 experience points in it.

name: Medicine
description: Academic Ability; the Third Ring of Solomon grants 100 experience points in it.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Academic Ability; a score of 4 is needed to read the alphabets of the Ars Notoria text.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Academic Ability known by the Franciscan Teacher and taught by the Patron Angel.

name: Orthodox Church Lore
description: Lore Ability of the Byzantine Priest.

name: Holy Land Lore
description: Lore Ability of the Knight Templar template.

name: University Lore
description: Lore Ability of the Franciscan Teacher template.

name: Magic Lore
description: Arcane Ability; Pagans may begin with it.

name: Faerie Lore
description: Arcane Ability; Pagans may begin with it.

name: Infernal Lore
description: Arcane Ability held by the Curious Nun.

name: Concentration
description: Ability used to keep focus when distracted during Holy Music; required of Perfecti.

name: Music
description: Ability rolled with Presence to sing a devotional song for Holy Music.

name: Teaching
description: Ability; the Franciscan Teacher is a skilled teacher and the Patron Angel teaches.

name: Holy Method of Meditation
description: Holy Method with which the Holy Music Ability is associated.

name: The Cantores
description: Primarily Christian holy tradition dedicated to worshipping God through music, gathering in cities and great abbeys; opposed to bawdy secular music.

name: Priory of Saint Nerius
description: Secret holy societas of Hermetic magi following a modified Benedictine Rule, seeking Nerius's canonization; its central house lies in the mountains of northern Italy.

name: Perfecti
description: Mythic Companion type: dualist holy men and women of Southern France, leaders of the Cathars, required to take Enemies (the Church) and Perfectus.

name: Cathars
description: Followers of the Perfecti in Southern France professing dualist doctrine contrary to Roman practice.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Hermetic order of magi; Nerius is considered its patron saint.

name: House Criamon
description: Hermetic House to which the saintly magus Nerius belonged.

name: The Church
description: The Latin Church, which Neriusians petition and Perfecti oppose; it views Ars Notoria as holy.

name: Eastern Church
description: Orthodox church which allows married men to become priests.

name: Franciscan Order
description: Mendicant order; the Neriusians are adapting to the Franciscan movement and the Franciscan Teacher joined it.

name: Benedictine Rule
description: Monastic rule followed in modified form by the Priory of Saint Nerius.

name: Knights Templar
description: Military order whose knight has sworn to own no property and looks after the order's European interests.

name: Quraysh
description: Dominant tribe of Mecca, guardians of the Ka'ba sanctuary, to which Muhammad belonged.

name: Umayyads
description: Caliphal dynasty (r. 660-750); the Umayyad caliph's forces killed al-Husayn.

name: 'Abbasids
description: Caliphal dynasty ruling from 750 to the present from Baghdad; they received Dhu'l-Fiqar.

name: Mu'tazilis
description: Muslim theological school stressing free will and a created Qur'an; briefly favored then banned in 1017 and 1041.

name: Sunnis
description: Mainstream Muslims whose doctrines follow al-Ash'ari and al-Maturidi; they recognize the caliph in Baghdad.

name: Shi'is
description: Muslims supporting the claims of 'Ali's family, following a line of imams and giving greater role to reason.

name: Sufis
description: Muslim mystics seeking union with God through asceticism and group ritual, gathering in tariqas.

name: Hanafis
description: Madhhab (school of Islamic law) founded by Abu Hanifa.

name: Malikis
description: Madhhab founded by Malik ibn Anas, followed by most Sunni jurists under the Almohads.

name: Shafi'is
description: Madhhab founded by Muhammad al-Shafi'i.

name: Hanbalis
description: Madhhab founded by Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

name: Twelver Shi'is
description: Most numerous Shi'i division, recognizing twelve imams, the last in occultation until he returns as mahdi.

name: Isma'ilis
description: Shi'i movements recognizing Isma'il's son Muhammad as seventh imam; includes the Qarmatians and Fatimids.

name: Qarmatians
description: Revolutionary Isma'ili group found in Iraq and Arabia.

name: Fatimids
description: Isma'ili dynasty ruling North Africa and Egypt from the 10th century until 1171, claiming to be imams and rightful caliphs.

name: Assassins
description: Nizari Isma'ili sect founded by Hasan-i Sabbah at Alamut, hierarchically organized and known for political assassination.

name: Almohads
description: Current rulers of Muslim Spain and North Africa, whose doctrine blends Sunni, Shi'i and Mu'tazili elements; founded by Ibn Tumart.

name: Sabeans
description: Star-worshipping cult of Harran, Syria, once granted dhimmi status.

name: 'Ulama'
description: The religious elite of Muslim society, sing. 'alim.

name: Tariqa
description: Sufi group usually based at a convent or saint's tomb, led by a shaykh.

name: Church Deacon
description: Grog template: a proud deacon who assists the parish priest and reads from the Bible.

name: Curious Nun
description: Grog template: an herbalist nun who broke her vows, charmed by a Hermetic covenant.

name: Pious Warrior
description: Grog template: a mace-wielding covenant warrior protected by a saintly relic necklace.

name: Byzantine Priest
description: Companion template: a married Eastern priest born in Constantinople who fled its sack.

name: Knight Templar
description: Companion template: a scarred Templar returned from the Holy Land who loves fighting and fine living.

name: Franciscan Teacher
description: Companion template: an indebted university master who became a Franciscan and seeks to convert pagans and the Order of Hermes.

name: Caliph
description: Successor to the Prophet, religious and secular leader of the Muslim state; nominal head for Sunnis in Baghdad.

name: Sultan
description: Governor of territories theoretically serving the caliph.

name: Imam
description: Prayer leader; for Shi'is also a divinely designated spiritual leader from the line of Muhammad.

name: Shaykh
description: Senior Sufi leading a tariqa; also a title of Assassin religious leaders.

name: Zahid
description: Particularly pious Sufi said to work miracles (karamas).

name: Mu'adhdhin
description: Caller who announces the call to prayer from a minaret.

name: Qadi
description: Muslim judge who may annul marriages; a religious-class role.

name: Mufti
description: Member of the Muslim religious classes.

name: Mamluk
description: Muslim slave-soldier role non-Muslims may not hold.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic magus; magi are exceptions to the Dhimmi requirement.

name: The Neriusian Portal
description: CrVi 65 holy ritual (R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Circle) creating a level 1 terrestrial regio around the caster; said to have been taught to Nerius by the angel Samuil.

name: Nerius
description: French magus of House Criamon considered the patron saint of the Order of Hermes; a stormcrow with a magical mantle, never canonized.

name: Samuil
description: Angel believed to have taught The Neriusian Portal to Nerius.

name: King Solomon
description: Most powerful magician of ancient times, who asked God for wisdom; source of the Ars Notoria.

name: Apollonius
description: Solomon's most ardent student, who recorded the Ars Notoria.

name: Michael
description: Archangel sent by God to grant Solomon divine knowledge.

name: Bonisagus
description: Hermetic founder, mentioned as long after Solomon.

name: Muhammad
description: Prophet of Islam born at Mecca c. 570, recipient of the Qur'an; the most revered holy forbear with Divine Might 100.

name: Khadija
description: Wealthy widow who employed and married Muhammad; his first wife.

name: 'A'isha
description: Probably Muhammad's favorite wife, in whose house he died.

name: al-Nasir
description: Current 'Abbasid caliph (acceded 1180) ruling vigorously from Baghdad.

name: al-Ash'ari
description: Theologian (d. 935) who shaped mainstream Sunni doctrine; author of Kitab al-Luma'.

name: al-Maturidi
description: Theologian (d. 944) whose doctrines are mainstream Sunni.

name: Israfil
description: Angel who will blow the trumpet twice on the Day of Judgment.

name: Dajjal
description: The Antichrist in Islamic belief, to be slain by Jesus.

name: Iblis
description: The devil, said by some to be a jinni who refused to bow to Adam; conqueror of Jinnistan.

name: Jesus
description: Prophet to whom scripture was given; taken directly to heaven and will slay Dajjal.

name: Abraham
description: Prophet and holy forbear (Divine Might 75), builder of the Ka'ba, buried at Hebron; a Greater Saint.

name: Isma'il
description: Son of Abraham whom he was prepared to sacrifice; ancestor of the Arabs.

name: Moses
description: Prophet given scripture; the location of his grave is unknown.

name: David
description: Prophet given scripture, buried in Jerusalem; may be invoked as a Greater Saint.

name: Adam
description: The earliest prophet; brought a shining jewel from Paradise.

name: al-Husayn
description: Grandson of Muhammad killed in 680, revered by Shi'is as an imam; holy forbear with Divine Might 75.

name: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib
description: Fourth caliph and son-in-law of Muhammad; first imam for the Shi'is, recipient of Dhu'l-Fiqar.

name: Rabi'a al-'Adawiyya
description: Early Muslim mystic of Basra, model for Sufis; holy forbear with Divine Might 50.

name: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i
description: Founder of the Shafi'i school of law (d. 820), buried in Cairo; holy forbear with Divine Might 25.

name: Nur al-Din
description: Famous Muslim counter-crusader (d. 1174) said taught wondrous powers by Khidr; holy forbear with Divine Might 25.

name: Saladin
description: Sultan zealous for the jihad who besieged Masyaf and was intimidated by Sinan.

name: Khidr
description: Immortal Muslim prophet, the Green One, who drank of the Water of Life and wanders giving advice.

name: Baha' al-Din ibn Shaddad
description: Friend and biographer of Saladin (d. 1234).

name: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz
description: Umayyad caliph (r. 717-20) credited with the pact of the dhimmis.

name: Abu Hanifa
description: Founder of the Hanafi school (d. 767).

name: Malik ibn Anas
description: Founder of the Maliki school (d. 795).

name: Ahmad ibn Hanbal
description: Founder of the Hanbali school (d. 855).

name: Fatima
description: Daughter of the Prophet, entombed at the Mosque of the Prophet.

name: Abu Bakr
description: First caliph, entombed at the Mosque of the Prophet; passed down the Prophet's seal ring.

name: 'Umar
description: Second caliph, entombed at the Mosque of the Prophet.

name: 'Uthman
description: Third caliph who dropped the Prophet's seal ring down a well in 650 and was later assassinated.

name: Gabriel
description: Angel who carried Muhammad on a heavenly steed from Mecca to Jerusalem.

name: al-Bukhari
description: Compiler of Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870).

name: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
description: Compiler of Sahih Muslim (d. 875).

name: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
description: Author of Jami' al-Bayan (d. 923).

name: Ibn Ishaq
description: Author of al-Sira al-Nabawiyya, a biography of the Prophet.

name: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali
description: Great Sufi and theologian (d. 1111), author of Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din.

name: Farid al-Din 'Attar
description: Persian mystical poet and author of Tadhkirat al-Awliya'.

name: al-Shaykh al-Mufid
description: Author of Kitab al-Irshad (d. 1022).

name: al-Junayd
description: Early writer at the origins of Sufism (d. 910).

name: al-Hallaj
description: Early Sufi writer executed for heresy for claiming to be God incarnate (d. 922).

name: Abu Nasr al-Sarraj
description: Writer who formalized Sufi theory (d. 988).

name: Ibn 'Arabi
description: Mystical poet of Damascus, currently the most active Sufi thinker.

name: al-Hasan al-'Askari
description: Eleventh Twelver imam, died 874.

name: Muhammad al-Mahdi
description: Twelfth imam of the Twelvers, in occultation until he returns as the mahdi.

name: Ja'far al-Sadiq
description: Sixth Shi'i imam (d. 765).

name: Hasan-i Sabbah
description: Persian Fatimid propagandist who seized Alamut in 1090 and founded the Assassins.

name: al-Mustansir
description: Fatimid caliph who died in 1094 after nominating Nizar.

name: Nizar
description: Eldest son of al-Mustansir, ousted and murdered; the Assassins sided with him.

name: al-Musta'li
description: Younger son of al-Mustansir installed as Fatimid caliph over Nizar.

name: Rashid al-Din Sinan
description: Greatest master of the Syrian Assassins (r. 1162-c.1193), said to be a magician; threatened Saladin.

name: Ibn Tumart
description: Founder of the Almohads who proclaimed himself the mahdi c. 1121.

name: Jinn
description: Intelligent race made of smokeless flame; some embrace Islam, others tempt humans. In Ars Magica they are faerie creatures.

name: Angel
description: Beings made of light, God's direct servants; the Fourth Ring of Solomon summons a lesser angel as guide.

name: Demon
description: Infernal beings; they cannot hide their nature from the Fifth Ring and suffer from the shahada and zakat.

name: Mecca
description: Native city of Muhammad and site of the haram and Ka'ba; its Dominion auras are one point stronger.

name: Medina
description: Oasis formerly Yathrib that welcomed Muhammad; site of the Mosque of the Prophet.

name: Ka'ba
description: Shrine of the Black Stone in Mecca built by Abraham and Isma'il; Dominion aura 10.

name: Haram
description: Sanctuary area around the Ka'ba at Mecca, direction of prayer.

name: Mosque of the Prophet
description: First mosque, in Medina, housing the tombs of Muhammad, Fatima, Abu Bakr and 'Umar; Dominion aura 9.

name: Dome of the Rock
description: Shrine in Jerusalem housing the rock from which Muhammad ascended; Dominion aura 10.

name: Aqsa Mosque
description: Important mosque on the Temple Mount with a Dominion aura of 6.

name: Temple Mount
description: Site in Jerusalem of supreme holiness to Jews and Muslims.

name: Western Wall
description: Remnant of the Jewish Temple, with a Dominion aura of 10.

name: Jerusalem
description: Holy city containing the Temple Mount and David's tomb.

name: Mount of Olives
description: Site outside Jerusalem where Rabi'a is buried.

name: Hebron
description: Site of the Cave of the Patriarchs, tomb of Abraham.

name: Karbala'
description: Site of al-Husayn's burial.

name: Cairo
description: City where al-Husayn's head and al-Shafi'i are interred.

name: Basra
description: Home town of Rabi'a al-'Adawiyya.

name: Damascus
description: City of Nur al-Din's tomb and home of Ibn 'Arabi.

name: Baghdad
description: Seat of the 'Abbasid caliph.

name: Constantinople
description: Byzantine capital, birthplace of the Byzantine Priest, sacked when he was 15.

name: Ctesiphon
description: Persian capital in Iraq.

name: Arabian Peninsula
description: Birthplace of Islam, inhabited by oasis cultivators and nomads.

name: Mountains of Qaf
description: Homeland of the jinn thought to surround the world, likely within Arcadia.

name: Jinnistan
description: Subterranean homeland of the jinn conquered by Iblis.

name: Arcadia
description: Faerie realm; Neriusians hold it is the Garden of Eden, and jinn homelands likely lie within it.

name: Garden of Eden
description: Which the Neriusians maintain is Arcadia, where humanity was created.

name: University of Paris
description: Suspected location of a copy of Ars Notoria.

name: Bishop of Armagh's library
description: Library in Ireland suspected to hold a copy of Ars Notoria.

name: Alamut
description: Fortress in northern Persia seized by Hasan-i Sabbah, seat of the Assassins.

name: Masyaf
description: Most important Syrian fortress of the Assassins, besieged by Saladin in 1176.

name: Harran
description: City in Syria home of the Sabeans.

name: Alexandria
description: Where Nizar was murdered in prison.

name: al-Safa and al-Marwa
description: Two hillocks at Mecca between which pilgrims run.

name: Mina
description: Site of the hajj where pilgrims stone a column representing Satan.

name: 'Arafat
description: Plain east of Mina where the 'standing' of the hajj occurs.

name: Muzdalifa
description: Stopping place between 'Arafat and Mina during the hajj.

name: Holy Land
description: Where the Knight Templar fought.

name: Janna
description: Paradise, the blissful gardens.

name: Jahannam
description: Outer circle of hell, a purgatory for guilty Muslims.

name: Empyreal realm
description: Realm to which Nerius could travel through his greater regio spell.

name: Iberian Tribunal
description: Hermetic tribunal including large territory under Muslim rule.

name: Levant Tribunal
description: Hermetic tribunal including large territory under Muslim rule.

name: Divine
description: Realm within which Ars Notoria operates; its powers are Divine.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine aura of human faith; Muslim Dominion auras rise during prayer, Ramadan and holidays.

name: Infernal
description: Realm of demons, pained by the shahada and zakat.

name: Magic
description: Realm whose lore Pagans may start with.

name: Faerie
description: Realm to which jinn belong in Ars Magica.

name: The Book of Solomon
description: Book containing the Ars Notoria.

name: The Keys of Solomon
description: Book containing the Ars Notoria.

name: Ars Notoria text
description: Apollonius's text in four languages, a Quality 20 tractatus, the only way to initially learn Ars Notoria.

name: Prophet's Seal Ring
description: Silver seal ring of Muhammad lost down a well by 'Uthman; would be a relic of Faith 7 and Divine Might 70.

name: Dhu'l-Fiqar
description: Two-pointed sword of the Prophet given to 'Ali; relic with Divine Might 70 that puts out enemies' eyes.

name: Qur'an
description: Muslim holy book compiled from revelations to Muhammad; a Summa of Theology: Islam and can be invoked for baraka.

name: Jami' al-Bayan 'an Ta'wil al-Qur'an
description: Massive commentary on the Qur'an by al-Tabari; Summa on Theology: Islam and Islamic Law.

name: Kitab al-Luma'
description: Tractatus by al-Ash'ari defending mainstream theology against the Mu'tazilis.

name: al-Risala
description: Treatise on Islamic jurisprudence by al-Shafi'i.

name: al-Sahihan
description: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, the two most respected hadith collections.

name: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya
description: Biography of the Prophet by Ibn Ishaq.

name: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din
description: Summa by al-Ghazali uniting mainstream doctrine with Sufi inspiration.

name: Tadhkirat al-Awliya'
description: Biographies of Muslim mystics by Farid al-Din 'Attar, with altered sources.

name: Kitab al-Irshad
description: Biography of the twelve imams by al-Shaykh al-Mufid.

name: Water of Life
description: Water which made Khidr immortal.

name: Rings of Solomon
description: Seven levels of Ars Notoria wisdom, each a combination of orations and notae, learned in order.

name: Notae
description: Individual Ars Notoria formulas.

name: Orations
description: Ars Notoria prayers recited in original languages at specific times.

name: Recitation Score
description: Intelligence + Ars Notoria + modifiers; plus a stress die gives the recitation total.

name: First Ring of Solomon
description: Grants 100 experience points in Philosophiae and +3 Communication; recited in Spring or Autumn.

name: Second Ring of Solomon
description: Grants 100 experience points in Theology and +3 Intelligence; recited in Winter.

name: Third Ring of Solomon
description: Grants 100 experience points in Medicine and Greater Purifying Touch.

name: Fourth Ring of Solomon
description: Summons a personal Patron Angel as guide and teacher.

name: Fifth Ring of Solomon
description: Allows sensing the realm affiliation of beings; recited in Summer.

name: Sixth Ring of Solomon
description: Grants holy divination of God's plan; recited in Spring.

name: Seventh Ring of Solomon
description: Grants perfect understanding; no botches and all simple rolls become stress rolls.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural layered area; The Neriusian Portal creates a level 1 terrestrial regio.

name: Divine Aura
description: Aura of the Divine; Ars Notoria reduces its casting penalty.

name: Realm Interaction Chart
description: Chart of penalties for casting in auras of other realms.

name: The Gift
description: Supernatural talent; baptism is believed to impair it, and only Gifted readers can learn Ars Notoria.

name: Vis
description: Magical resource monastic magi cannot own.

name: Familiar
description: Bound magical companion; monastic vows may prohibit binding one.

name: Twilight
description: Hermetic Twilight; the Seventh Ring spares one Twilight points from botches.

name: Warping
description: Warping Points, not gained from Divine auras while a ring is active.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Resistance a Fifth Ring roll must exceed to identify a creature's realm.

name: True Name
description: Name used in supernatural activities; baptism or Muslim birth rites render it unusable.

name: Faith Points
description: Divine resource; a completed hajj grants 3 Faith Points.

name: Confidence
description: Confidence Score and Points; copying the Qur'an grants a Confidence Point.

name: Divine Might
description: Measure of a holy figure's or relic's divine power.

name: Greater Saint
description: Saint category to which Abraham and David belong.

name: Holy Forbears
description: Muslim revered figures at whose shrines baraka may be invoked, similar to saints.

name: Baraka
description: Blessing sought by Muslims at the tombs of holy forbears.

name: Khawass al-Qur'an
description: Special properties of the Qur'an, which may be invoked anywhere; Divine Might 100.

name: Saints
description: Christian holy figures invoked for miracles, a model for Muslim holy forbears.

name: Shari'a
description: Islamic law derived from the usul al-fiqh.

name: Usul al-fiqh
description: The principles of jurisprudence: Qur'an, Sunna, ijma' and qiyas.

name: Sunna
description: Actions and sayings of the Prophet and companions as examples of good behavior.

name: Hadith
description: Individual narrative reports of the Prophet; also the collective literature.

name: Ijma'
description: Consensus of the community, in practice legal scholars.
